# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 86 (Bi-Vb Pc86)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc86  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 86  
**Title (English, from literature):** Wearing a hip ornament  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅghāṇi Sutta* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 86) sets forth the rule that a nun who wears a decorative hip ornament (*saṅghāṇi*) commits an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the Theravāda nun's Vinaya, Ute Hüsken observes that this rule likely addresses a decorative belt worn specifically by laywomen, accounting for the absence of an equivalent rule in the monks' Vinaya [Hüsken 1997]. While ordinary waistbands (*kāyabandhana*) worn over the robes were obligatory for both monks and nuns, simpler hip-threads (*kaṭisuttaka*)—though prohibited for monks in the *Cullavagga*—are permitted to nuns within the non-offense clause (*anāpatti*) of this rule [Hüsken 1997]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Curated parallels for this rule in the Theravāda tradition include the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pācittiya 86) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pācittiya 86), alongside Chinese Vinaya parallels in the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 156* and its Pātimokkha counterpart) and Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 157* and its Pātimokkha counterpart) traditions.
